tagline: Patrick Henry's last speech, and the road to his last home.
intro: Route 40 leaves Charlotte Court House and heads west, six miles to the little town of Phenix. Then Mount Calvary Road and Patrick Henry Road carry it over into Campbell County and on toward Red Hill, where Patrick Henry spent his last years.
A second run starts in Drakes Branch and takes the back roads, Saxkey and Hermon and Mulberry Hill, then River Road down toward Randolph, near the Staunton River.

moments.title: Randolph
moments.text: In June 1864, 938 men held the Staunton River railroad bridge near Randolph, helped by a train run back and forth to look like reinforcements.

moments.title: Charlotte Court House
moments.text: Patrick Henry gave his last political speech here in March 1799, in a town that went by The Magazine, Daltonsburgh, Marysville and Smithville before it took the courthouse's name.

moments.title: Red Hill
moments.text: Henry retired to this Staunton River tobacco plantation in 1794 and is buried here, beside his law office and a reconstruction of his last house.
